prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures an open outdoor river scene where a continuous gradient on the water surface transitions from bright white within arm's reach (under 1 metre) at the bottom foreground to dark black across the wide river channel and distant wooded hills (over 100 metres away) in front and to the right. On the left side, a riverbank tree canopy overhanging the water is rendered in medium grey at roughly 3 to 10 metres from the camera wearer, becoming brighter and more prominent from frame 1 to frame 2 as the camera turns slightly left and drifts past the trees through frame 5. In the bottom-right corner of frames 1, 3, 4, and 5, brightest white regions (about 0.3 to 0.8 metres away, within the camera wearer's arm's reach) correspond to the partly cropped legs/limbs of a person and the edge of a blue watercraft or float in frame 5, though no full person or face orientation is visible in view. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map clarifies the smooth receding plane of the turbulent water and separates the near left-bank foliage (3–10 metres) from the far background ridge, which blend together in dark greens in RGB. However, the depth map is unreliable around the fine upper tree branches against the sky (creating jagged grey-and-black halo artifacts), collapses the distant hills and sky into identical zero-depth black, and blurs the boundary between the foreground person/boat and the adjacent water.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is almost entirely black and fails to segment the river, left-bank trees (3 to 10 metres away), sky, or the blue watercraft edge visible within arm's reach (about 0.5 metres) at the bottom-right of frame 5. It detects only a single "person" mask in the bottom-right corner of frame 1 and a smaller clipped "person" mask in the same corner of frame 3, corresponding to the camera wearer's or a companion's bare knees/legs and hand situated roughly 0.3 to 0.8 metres in front of and below the camera. Because only the lower extremities and a hand in frame 1 enter the bottom-right frame boundary while the rest of the body is occluded/out of view behind or below the camera, neither body facing direction nor gaze toward the camera wearer can be determined, though the visible limbs remain within arm's reach. Across the five frames, this bottom-right body part shifts partly out of view in frame 2, reappears slightly in frames 3 and 4, and sits next to the unsegmented blue watercraft edge in frame 5 as the camera turns slightly right again. While the segmentation mask explicitly labels the heavily cropped foreground shapes in frames 1 and 3 as human body parts—which are shadowed and easy to miss in the RGB corner—it is highly unreliable because it misses the same limb in frames 4 and 5, merges the two legs and hand into a single coarse blob in frame 1, and leaves the entire surrounding environment unlabelled.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely black across all five frames, detecting zero body or hand keypoints anywhere in the scene. In the RGB context, the scene consists of open river water stretching from under 1 metre in front of the camera wearer to distant tree-lined hills over 100 metres ahead, bordered by overhanging trees 3 to 10 metres to the left that pass alongside the viewpoint across the five frames. The only human presence is a heavily cropped limb and hand in the bottom-right corner at roughly 0.3 to 0.8 metres (within arm's reach, beside a blue watercraft edge in frame 5), with the person's torso and head completely out of view below and behind the camera so that facing direction and gaze are unobservable. The pose map offers no spatial information beyond the RGB strip and is unreliable for extreme close-up, heavily truncated limbs at the frame boundary, failing to detect the visible hand and leg in frame 1 or the partial leg segments in frames 3 through 5.
